response.title: Is it better to run Starlink from my camper's own battery or from a separate power station when boondocking?
response.answer:
For most boondocking setups, I'd recommend running Starlink from your camper's house battery—provided you have a decent lithium battery bank and solar charging.

A separate portable power station makes more sense if your camper has a small battery, you want to protect your remaining power for essential systems, or you frequently use Starlink away from the camper.

The biggest factor isn't necessarily which battery you use. It's how efficiently you power Starlink and how much usable battery capacity you have.

One important distinction: Using your camper's inverter to power Starlink through a standard AC adapter may waste more energy than powering Starlink directly from a properly regulated DC supply.

A power station with a DC output can sometimes outperform a camper's inverter setup, even if the camper has a larger battery.

4. What I'd do for boondocking

If your camper has 200 Ah or more of LiFePO4 battery capacity and solar panels, I'd normally connect Starlink to the house system, preferably through a compatible, properly fused DC power connection.

If you only have a 100 Ah lead-acid battery, I'd lean toward a separate power station to preserve power for your refrigerator, lights, water pump, and other essentials.

If you use Starlink for remote work, having a separate power station as a backup is especially useful, even when your main power comes from the camper.

5. Three questions that would help me recommend the best setup

Which Starlink do you have? Mini or regular Standard?

What's your camper battery setup? For example, 100 Ah lithium, 200 Ah lithium, or AGM.

Do you have solar panels? If so, how many watts?

With those details, I can compare the actual runtime, charging needs, and whether buying a separate power station would be worthwhile for your camper.

| Factor | Camper house battery | Separate power station |
|---|---|---|
| Energy efficiency | Excellent with direct DC power | Good with DC; less efficient with AC |
| Battery capacity | Often larger, especially with lithium | Depends on station size |
| Solar charging | Uses camper's existing solar | May require separate charging |

| Portability | Limited | Excellent |
| Cost | Usually cheaper if already installed | Additional purchase |
| Best for | Full-time or frequent boondocking | Occasional trips, backup, portability |

**One important distinction:** Using your camper's inverter to power Starlink through a standard AC adapter may waste more energy than powering Starlink directly from a properly regulated DC supply.

A power station with a DC output can sometimes outperform a camper's inverter setup, even if the camper has a larger battery.

## 2. How much battery will Starlink consume?

Starlink's official average power figures vary by model. <Cite refs={["turn543501search0","turn543501search1"]}/>

| Starlink model | Average draw | Energy for 8 hours |
|---|---:|---:|
| Starlink Mini | 20–40 W | 160–320 Wh |
| Standard (Gen 3/4) | 75–100 W | 600–800 Wh |
| Older Standard Actuated | 50–75 W | 400–600 Wh |

These figures don't include additional losses from your camper's inverter.

## 3. Estimate your Starlink runtime

Use this calculator to see how much battery Starlink would consume during a boondocking trip.

{@body const [capacity,setCapacity] = DIL.useState(100)}
{@body const [battery,setBattery] = DIL.useState("lifepo4")}
{@body const [starlink,setStarlink] = DIL.useState("mini")}
{@body const [hours,setHours] = DIL.useState(8)}
{@body const [connection,setConnection] = DIL.useState("dc")}
{@body const watts = starlink==="mini"?30:starlink==="standard"?85:65}
{@body const usable = capacity*12.8*(battery==="lifepo4"?0.9:0.5)}
{@body const eff = connection==="dc"?0.95:0.85}
{@body const daily = watts*hours/eff}

    </grid-item>
    <grid-item>

    </grid-item>
    <grid-item>

      <select block value={connection} onChange={setConnection} options={[{label:"DC (95% efficient)",value:"dc"},{label:"AC inverter (85%)",value:"ac"}]}/>
    </grid-item>
  </grid>
  <row align="center" justify="between">
    **Starlink use per day**
    <text weight="medium" tabularNums>{hours} hours</text>
  </row>
  <slider min={1} max={24} step={1} value={hours} onChange={setHours}/>
  <divider color="subtle"/>
  <grid columns={2} gap={2}>
    <grid-item>
      <box background="surface-secondary" radius="lg" padding={3} gap={1}>

        <title size="xl" color="default" tabularNums>{Math.round(daily)} Wh</title>
        <caption>{Math.round(daily/usable*100)}% of usable capacity</caption>
      </box>
    </grid-item>
    <grid-item>
      <box background="surface-secondary" radius="lg" padding={3} gap={1}>
        <text color="secondary" size="xs">Starlink-only runtime</text>
        <title size="xl" color="default" tabularNums>{(usable*eff/watts).toFixed(1)} hrs</title>
        <caption>From a full battery</caption>
      </box>
    </grid-item>
  </grid>
  <box gap={1}>
    <row height="10px" background="surface-tertiary" radius="full" clip>
      <box background={daily/usable>0.8?"danger-solid":"rgba(34,139,100,0.85)"} width={`${Math.min(100,daily/usable*100)}%`} radius="full"/>
    </row>
    <caption>Illustrative estimate using a 12.8 V battery, with 90% usable lithium capacity or 50% usable lead-acid capacity. Assumes no solar charging or other camper loads; inverter idle draw may further reduce runtime.</caption>
  </box>
</box>
